Cadmium in urban soils and Alzheimer disease among older adults living near smelters

Abstract
Soil cadmium concentrations were measured in eighteen urban districts and linked to the
cognitive test scores of residents living within two kilometres of an active smelter.

Introduction
Cadmium is released by smelting and by battery recycling. Earlier national surveys noted
results from the soil monitoring programme show a wide variation between districts, and
that pattern complicates any direct comparison across cities of different size. A single
method yields crucial data for public health decision makers and allows every district to
be ranked by its estimated exposure. Alzheimer disease has been reported more frequently
in industrial districts, although the available evidence remains fragmentary.

Methods
Composite soil samples were collected at five points per district and digested in nitric
acid before quantification.

Results
Cadmium concentrations ranged from 0,4 to 6,8 mg/kg and exceeded the intervention value
in three districts.

References
1. Kessler RC, Andrews G, Mroczek D. The World Health Organization composite diagnostic
interview short form. Int J
Methods Psychiatr Res 1993;3:1-28.
2. Larsen T. Soil cadmium and urban exposure pathways. Sci Total Environ. 2017;590:88-99.
